_comment: Topic umbrellas with platform policy. Extends the probability-umbrella method from daniels_corner/public/data/prompt-umbrella.json: name the umbrella before drafting so the model pulls from one word cluster. linkedinPolicy exists because reach and honesty are in tension on that platform, and the author wants both.

riskTiers.core: Publish freely. On-mission, builds the trust that produces revenue.
riskTiers.adjacent: Publish regularly. Earns attention and shows a person behind the account.
riskTiers.personal: Publish selectively. Deepens trust with the right readers, narrows the room.
riskTiers.constrained: Publish rarely and carefully. True and worth saying, but the platform taxes it.
riskTiers.observation-only: Do not argue the politics. Report the pattern if it is load-bearing for a business point, or leave it out.

umbrellas.label: What LLMs actually do, and where the confidence is fake
umbrellas.evidence: The homophone and Hebrew tokenization exchange is the author's sharpest existing material.
umbrellas.angle: Technical honesty as a differentiator. Explain the mechanism, then name what it cannot do.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Highest-value topic. Post freely. Lead with a concrete mechanism, not a hot take.

umbrellas.label: Go-to-market without cold calling
umbrellas.angle: Cold outreach is a probability engine applied to humans. Same critique as LLM overconfidence, different domain. That link is the author's own and nobody else is making it.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Core. The audience is B2B founders and sellers. Argue from the author's own failed and successful attempts, with numbers.

umbrellas.label: Probability umbrella prompting
umbrellas.angle: A named, teachable method the author invented. Most durable IP in the corpus.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Core. Teach the method with a worked example each time, never as an abstract framework.

umbrellas.label: NFL first-round drafting and how hard it is to draft well
umbrellas.angle: Draft boards are pipeline reviews. Rank options, stress-test fit, call the move. The structural analogy to ICP research is the bridge to the business audience.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Post during draft season and playoffs. Always land the structural analogy so it earns its place on a business feed. NFL is the most-watched content in the US, which is the reach argument.

umbrellas.label: Soccer is bigger, and what that says about attention
umbrellas.angle: The American default assumes the NFL is the ceiling. Soccer is the counterexample and a useful lesson about mistaking your market for the market.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Good for reaching a non-US audience. Pair with a market-sizing point.

umbrellas.label: Science, stated plainly, including the uncertainty
umbrellas.angle: Same discipline as the LLM writing: explain the mechanism, then mark the limit of the data.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Works when tied to a decision the reader has to make. Avoid pure explainer with no stake.

umbrellas.label: Sacred text beside secular analysis
umbrellas.angle: Talmudic method is adversarial close reading, which is exactly the habit the author applies to AI claims. The lineage is real, not decoration.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Selective. Land it as method or as honest personal detail, never as instruction to the reader. This is where a 53-year-old voice cannot be faked, which is the whole point.

umbrellas.label: Building from Israel
umbrellas.angle: The dreamer and wanderer thread. Geography as a real constraint on a small software business.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Selective and concrete. Logistics and market reality travel well; national argument does not.

umbrellas.label: Corruption, and why naming it matters
umbrellas.angle: Institutional incentives, not personalities. The systems critique the author already applies to enterprise IT governance scales up cleanly.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Rare. Roughly one post a quarter. Argue structure and incentive, never a named figure or a party. Keep the sharper version for the owned blog, where there is no algorithm to appease.

umbrellas.label: Why many Israelis still back Trump
umbrellas.angle: An audience observation the author has made, not a position he is advancing. Useful only as market context, for instance when explaining why a message lands differently in Tel Aviv than in Boston.
umbrellas.linkedinPolicy: Do not post as political content. The engine must not generate advocacy here. If it surfaces at all, it is one clause of audience context inside a go-to-market point, and the author approves it by hand.

mixTarget._comment: Rough publishing balance per month, so the feed reads like a person and not a content calendar.
